claim_being_audited: The current release can be certified now because aggregate launch readiness passes, there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and the HR benefits enrollment regression can be handled through current-release disclosure while prior approval and monitoring context support continuity.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results.
Material segment weaknesses for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring notes may provide context but cannot substitute for current evidence, reviewed mitigation, or approved risk acceptance.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support readiness but do not waive the disclosure or mitigation requirement.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release model card or equivalent release documentation showing the latest evaluation results, including the HR benefits enrollment regression.
Provide the exact disclosure language for the named launch use case affected by the HR benefits enrollment weakness and evidence that it is part of the release documentation.
If disclosure is not complete, provide approved risk acceptance or reviewed mitigation documentation that satisfies policy before launch.
Provide the materiality determination, if one exists, for why the HR benefits enrollment regression is or is not treated as a material limitation for the named use case.
specific_concerns: The policy condition for certification is not satisfied by the current record unless the current release documentation already reflects the latest evaluation results and discloses the HR benefits enrollment weakness, and no such documentation is in evidence.
The informal monitoring comment is explicitly not a reviewed mitigation, approved risk acceptance, or attached disclosure artifact.
The prior approval is stale relative to the current retrieval configuration change and current evaluation batch, so it cannot carry the present certification decision.
The actor's packet depends on a disclosure-based theory of compliance, but admissible evidence shows only that disclosure is required, not that it has actually been completed for this release.
unsupported_claims: The action to certify the model now is not evidentially supported because no admissible artifact shows the current release documentation reflects the HR benefits enrollment regression.
The packet's practical conclusion that certification is presently supportable on a narrow current-evidence basis overstates what the admissible record proves.
Any implication that manual post-launch monitoring can substitute for approved mitigation or disclosure is unsupported by the record.
